skill.name: genlayer-cli
skill.description: Guide agents through GenLayer CLI workflows for network setup, account management, contract deployment, interaction, and transaction debugging.
skill.summary: Use GenLayer CLI commands to manage networks, accounts, intelligent contracts, and transaction diagnostics.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are Markdown documentation false positives, but several documented CLI actions are real state-changing or secret-handling risks. The highest concern is guidance around private keys and passwords in command-line workflows.

remediation.issue: Password and private-key examples encourage command-line secret handling.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend keychain, keystore prompts, or secret managers. Warn users not to place real private keys or passwords in prompts, shell history, or process arguments.

remediation.issue: State-changing commands can deploy contracts, send funds, appeal transactions, reset local databases, or modify validators.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation guidance before deploy, write, send, appeal, reset, validator delete, and configuration changes.

remediation.issue: Global package installation changes the user environment and runs third-party package code.
remediation.suggestion: Suggest verifying the package source and version before installation, and prefer project-local or sandboxed installation when possible.

remediation.issue: The faucet URL is hardcoded in documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify the official GenLayer domain before using faucet pages or entering addresses.

content.value_statement: GenLayer development requires precise CLI steps for accounts, networks, deployment, and receipts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe GenLayer CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains GenLayer network selection for localnet, StudioNet, and testnets.
Guides account listing, creation, import, locking, unlocking, and token sending.
Provides deployment steps for single contracts and deploy folder workflows.
Supports read calls, write transactions, schema inspection, and source inspection.
Helps inspect receipts, stdout, stderr, and transaction lifecycle status.
Documents local Studio startup, reset, validator, and configuration commands.
limitations: Requires the GenLayer CLI to be installed and available in the shell.
Cannot claim faucet funds because the faucet requires browser verification.
State-changing commands can spend funds, deploy contracts, or modify local services.
Private keys and passwords require careful handling outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Contract
use_cases.description: Set the target network, prepare the active account, deploy a contract, and inspect the resulting transaction receipt.

use_cases.title: Debug Failed Transactions
use_cases.description: Check receipt output, compare lifecycle status with execution success, and decide whether contract code or infrastructure needs attention.

use_cases.title: Manage Local Testing
use_cases.description: Start local Studio, reset local state when needed, and manage local validators for repeatable test scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GenLayer CLI skill to check my current network and active account. Explain what each result means before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy One Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GenLayer CLI skill to deploy my contract from contracts/my_contract.py. Confirm the network and account first, then inspect the receipt.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Failed Transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GenLayer CLI skill to debug this transaction hash. Check execution output, lifecycle status, schema availability, and likely next action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Local Validator Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GenLayer CLI skill to plan a local Studio test with multiple validators, a clean database, contract deployment, and receipt verification.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy a GenLayer contract on testnet.
output: A short checklist confirms the selected network, active account, available balance, and contract path.
The response identifies which actions change network state and should be confirmed first.
After deployment, the response explains how to inspect the receipt and verify execution success.

output_examples.input: My transaction finalized but no contract appears.
output: The response separates lifecycle status from execution success.
It directs attention to receipt output before assuming a network or indexer issue.
It explains that failed execution can finalize without creating contract state.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare a local validator test.
output: The response outlines local Studio startup, optional database reset, validator count checks, and deployment validation.
It warns which steps can delete local state or change validator configuration.

best_practices: Confirm the target network before any deploy, write, send, appeal, or reset action.
Inspect receipt stdout and stderr before diagnosing missing schema or missing code.
Use keychain or secure secret storage instead of pasting private keys or passwords.
anti_patterns: Do not assume finalized transactions mean contract execution succeeded.
Do not batch many StudioNet writes without throttling and receipt checks.
Do not pass real private keys or reusable passwords in prompts or shell history.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps use the GenLayer CLI for networks, accounts, deployments, contract calls, receipts, local Studio, and validators.

faq.question: Does it install the GenLayer CLI?
faq.answer: It documents the installation command, but users should review package trust and environment impact before installing global tools.

faq.question: Can it claim faucet funds?
faq.answer: No. The faucet requires browser verification, so the user must claim funds manually.

faq.question: Can it run state-changing commands?
faq.answer: Yes, when the agent has shell access and the user approves the action. Deploy, write, send, appeal, and reset commands can change state.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use secure key storage where possible. Avoid putting private keys or passwords in prompts, command arguments, logs, or shell history.

faq.question: Why inspect receipts after finalization?
faq.answer: A transaction can be accepted or finalized while contract execution failed. Receipt output shows whether execution succeeded.
